title: Col. Richard Callaway of Boonesborough
summary: Richard Callaway helped blaze the path into Kentucky with Boone in 1775, co-founded Boonesborough, and defended the fort through the 1778 siege.
bodyMarkdown:
Richard Callaway was one of the first settlers of Boonesborough and one of its leading officers during the Revolutionary War. He shared the fort's hardest years with Daniel Boone, though not always on friendly terms. His life ended in an ambush outside the fort in 1780.

## From Virginia to the Kentucky River

An account of [Richard Callaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Callaway) says he was born on June 14, 1717, in Essex County, Virginia. In 1775 he joined Boone in marking the Wilderness Road into central Kentucky and became one of the founders of Boonesborough. He also helped organize the short-lived Transylvania Colony, the land venture behind the settlement.

## The 1776 kidnapping

On July 14, 1776, Callaway's daughters Elizabeth and Frances were captured with Jemima Boone while [canoeing near the fort](https://grokipedia.com/page/Boonesborough,_Kentucky). The raiders are described as a Cherokee and Shawnee party, and Callaway led one of the groups in the successful rescue. His nephew Flanders Callaway later married Jemima Boone.

## Burgess, colonel and accuser

In April 1777 Callaway and [John Todd](/stories/col-john-todd-of-lexington/) were elected burgesses for Kentucky County in the Virginia legislature. In June 1778 he became a justice of the peace and colonel of the county militia.

That September, a force under the Shawnee war chief [Blackfish](/stories/blackfish-cot-ta-wa-ma-go-chillicothe-war-chief/) [besieged Boonesborough from September 7 to 17](https://grokipedia.com/page/Siege_of_Boonesborough). Callaway helped lead the defense with Boone. After the siege, Callaway and [Benjamin Logan](/stories/benjamin-logan/) brought court-martial charges against Boone, claiming he had favored the British. Both men had nephews among the salt makers Boone surrendered earlier that year. The court acquitted Boone and then promoted him, which angered Callaway.

## Death in 1780

Callaway was killed by a Shawnee war party about a mile outside Boonesborough in 1780. The sources disagree on the day. One account of Callaway gives November 8, 1780, while an account of the [Siege of Boonesborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Boonesborough) gives March 8, 1780. Both agree that he was killed and scalped.

## Kentucky today

[Calloway County](https://grokipedia.com/page/Calloway_County,_Kentucky) in the Jackson Purchase was created from Hickman County in 1822 and named for him, though its spelling differs from his. Near Richmond, [Fort Boonesborough State Park](https://grokipedia.com/page/Fort_Boonesborough_State_Park) has a full-scale replica of the fort. It opened on September 30, 1974, on higher ground than the original site, which a short trail and markers connect to the replica. For more of the period, see the [Siege of Bryan's Station](/stories/bryan-station-siege-august-1782/) and [George Rogers Clark](/stories/george-rogers-clark/).
